newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks buttressed by select demand.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks buttressed by select demand.

text.p: Jordanian stocks finished comfortably ahead on Sunday with speculative trading on industrial Livestock and Poultry shares and outside buying on a major hotel share, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.14 percent, ending the day at 149.46 points in moderate volume of 1,103,450 dinars.

Brokers however fear the market may be running out of steam as most institutional investors remain on the sidelines and stocks have experienced profit-taking after the bourse's recent results-driven rally.
Industrials continued to dominate trade on Sunday.
Market leader Arab Bank, which propelled the index upwards in the first half of September, was shunned by investors in lacklustre activity.
Its stock, a major component of the official index, rose 3.00 dinars to 244 dinars in low trade worth 34,150 dinars that helped underpin overall trade.
Star performer Livestock and Poultry, which has been a focus of investor interest for the fourth week in a row, rose to 0.03 dinar to 0.90 dinars and dominated trading with turnover 383,343 dinars.
Most dealers said shareholders realising profit on their holdings kept up persistent speculative trade on the stock that has seen no fundamentals emerging to otherwise attract investors.
Other brokers say the stock is a target of a takeover attempt by a group of investors keen to buy a key stake.
Outside buying, said to be mostly foreign funds, appears to have pushed Arab International Hotels by 0.10 up to 5.00 dinars in healthy 238,837 dinar turnover.
Of 50 stocks traded, 19 fell, 14 advanced, and 17 closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange rose 0.14 percent to 82.67 points, still 13.45 percent down from the same time last year.
